title: Composition preserves the direct-image weight bound
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$, and an isomorphism $\iota:\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf C$. Use constructible $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$-Weil sheaves as in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], mixedness and upper weights as in [def-weil-punctual-weights], and $R^it_!=\mathcal H^i(Rt_!)$ for the compact-support functor of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]; higher direct images are indexed by $i\geq0$.

Let $h:X_0\to Z_0$ and $g:Z_0\to Y_0$ be separated finite-type
morphisms of $k_0$-schemes, where $Z_0$ and $Y_0$ are quasi-separated
$k_0$-schemes of finite type. Suppose the
direct-image weight assertion holds for $h$ and for $g$: for every
real $v$, every $\iota$-mixed Weil sheaf of weights at most $v$ on the
source has its $i$th higher direct image with compact support
$\iota$-mixed of weights at most $v+i$, for every $i$. Then the same
assertion holds for $gh$: if $\mathcal F$ is an $\iota$-mixed Weil
sheaf on $X_0$ of weights at most $w$, then $R^n(gh)_!\mathcal F$ is
$\iota$-mixed of weights at most $w+n$ for every $n$.

proof.text: Fix $w\in\mathbf R$, a constructible Weil sheaf $\mathcal F$ of weights at most $w$, and $n\geq0$. For each pair $a,b\geq0$ with $a+b=n$, the assumed assertion for $h$ gives that $R^bh_!\mathcal F$ is mixed of weights at most $w+b$. It is therefore an allowed input for the assertion for $g$, with the real parameter $v=w+b$. That assertion gives that $T_{a,b}=R^ag_!(R^bh_!\mathcal F)$ is mixed of weights at most $(w+b)+a=w+n$. These are direct applications of the two hypotheses; the equality uses $a+b=n$.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: weight bounds on E_2, its subquotients, and induction along the finite abutment filtration

proof.text: Apply [lem-zl-compact-support-leray-filtration] to $h,g,\mathcal F,n$. Its hypotheses are precisely our separated finite-type morphisms with quasi-separated finite-type intermediate and target schemes; it does not require mixedness. Write its filtration as $0=G_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq G_m=R^n(gh)_!\mathcal F$. For each $j$, it provides $a_j+b_j=n$ and Weil morphisms $S_j\hookrightarrow T_{a_j,b_j}$ and $S_j\twoheadrightarrow Q_j$, where $Q_j=G_j/G_{j-1}$. By step 1, $T_{a_j,b_j}$ is mixed of weights at most $w+n$. Clause (1) of [lem-a1-mixed-direct-summand] first applies to the subsheaf $S_j$ and then to its quotient $Q_j$. Thus every $Q_j$ is mixed of weights at most $w+n$. The filtration lemma supplies constructibility and Frobenius compatibility, so both applications take place in exactly the abelian category of Weil sheaves specified by the stability lemma.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph and second paragraph through stability under subquotients

proof.text: Induct on $j=0,\ldots,m$ to show that $G_j$ is mixed of weights at most $w+n$. For $j=0$, the zero sheaf has the empty filtration in [def-weil-punctual-weights], so the assertion holds for any real bound. For the induction step, $0\to G_{j-1}\to G_j\to Q_j\to0$ is exact by the definition of the successive quotient of the filtration from step 2. The induction hypothesis bounds $G_{j-1}$, and step 2 bounds $Q_j$. Clause (2) of [lem-a1-mixed-direct-summand] gives the same bound for $G_j$. At $j=m$ this is the required bound for $R^n(gh)_!\mathcal F$. Since $w,\mathcal F,n$ were arbitrary, the direct-image assertion holds for $gh$.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $h:X_0\to Z_0$ and $g:Z_0\to Y_0$ be separated finite-type
morphisms of $k_0$-schemes, where $Z_0$ and $Y_0$ are quasi-separated
$k_0$-schemes of finite type. Suppose the
direct-image weight assertion holds for $h$ and for $g$: for every
real $v$, every $\iota$-mixed Weil sheaf of weights at most $v$ on the
source has its $i$th higher direct image with compact support
$\iota$-mixed of weights at most $v+i$, for every $i$. Then the same
assertion holds for $gh$: if $\mathcal F$ is an $\iota$-mixed Weil
sheaf on $X_0$ of weights at most $w$, then $R^n(gh)_!\mathcal F$ is
$\iota$-mixed of weights at most $w+n$ for every $n$.

proof.text:
By [lem-zl-shriek-composition] there is a Frobenius-compatible
isomorphism $R(gh)_!\mathcal F\simeq Rg_!(Rh_!\mathcal F)$. Apply the
hypercohomology spectral sequence of the truncation construction
[def-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-filtrations] to the exact functor $Rg_!$
and the bounded complex $K=Rh_!\mathcal F$, whose cohomology sheaves
are $\mathcal H^b(K)=R^bh_!\mathcal F$. This is the compact-support
Leray spectral sequence

$$
E_2^{a,b}=R^ag_!\bigl(R^bh_!\mathcal F\bigr)
\ \Longrightarrow\ R^{a+b}(gh)_!\mathcal F,
$$

a spectral sequence of Weil sheaves (all maps are Frobenius-compatible,
[def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]), with only finitely many nonzero terms
and a finite abutment filtration
([lemma-weil-pbc-hypercohomology-convergence]).

By the assertion for $h$, the sheaf $R^bh_!\mathcal F$ is $\iota$-mixed
of weights at most $w+b$. By the assertion for $g$, applied with
$v=w+b$, the term $E_2^{a,b}$ is $\iota$-mixed of weights at most
$w+a+b$. Each later page $E_{r+1}^{a,b}$ is a subquotient of
$E_r^{a,b}$, so $E_\infty^{a,b}$ is a subquotient of $E_2^{a,b}$, and
the abutment $R^n(gh)_!\mathcal F$ carries a finite filtration whose
graded pieces are the $E_\infty^{a,b}$ with $a+b=n$; all of these are
constructible Weil sheaves and all maps are maps of Weil sheaves. For
$a+b=n$ the sheaf $E_2^{a,b}$ is $\iota$-mixed of weights at most
$w+n$, so by the sheaf-level stability of mixedness under Weil
subsheaves and quotients, [lem-a1-mixed-direct-summand](1), applied
page by page, so is $E_\infty^{a,b}$. Stability under extensions,
[lem-a1-mixed-direct-summand](2), applied along the finite filtration,
gives the same bound for $R^n(gh)_!\mathcal F$, in the sense of
[def-weil-punctual-weights].
